title: Dell XPS 14 (2026) tanıtıldı: Fiyatı ve özellikleri
summary: Dell'in yeni dizüstü bilgisayarı XPS 14 (2026), uzun pil ömrü, yenilenmiş tasarımı ve Intel'in en yeni işlemcileriyle tanıtıldı.
body:
XDA'nın aktardığına göre **Dell XPS 14** (2026), yenilenmiş alüminyum kasası, fiziksel fonksiyon tuşları ve yeni nesil Intel işlemcileriyle kullanıcı karşısına çıktı. Yaklaşık 1,3 kilogram ağırlığında ve 14,62 mm kalınlığında olan cihaz, taşınabilirliğinden ödün vermeden güçlü bir performans sunmayı hedefliyor. Modelin başlangıç fiyatı 2.249,99 dolar olarak açıklandı.

## Öne çıkan teknik özellikler ve pil ömrü

XDA'nın incelemesine göre bilgisayarın en büyük odak noktası enerji verimliliği ve pil ömrü oldu. Sektörde bir ilk olan 900ED pil hücresi teknolojisini kullanan 70Wh kapasiteli batarya, daha büyük bir kasa taşımadan yüksek enerji depolamayı başarıyor. XDA'nın aktardığına göre cihaz, Intel Core Ultra 7 işlemcili modelinde yapılan testlerde dikkat çekici süreler yakaladı.

- Intel Core Ultra Series 3 işlemci seçenekleri (Ultra X9 388H modeline kadar)
- 14 inç boyutunda 2K veya 2,8K OLED ekran seçenekleri
- 16 GB, 32 GB ve 64 GB LPDDR5x RAM alternatifleri

## Bağlantı seçenekleri ve tasarım

Cihazın tasarruf odaklı ekranı, güç tüketimini azaltmak için 1Hz ile 120Hz arasında değişen yenileme hızı sunuyor. Bağlantı tarafında ise üç adet Thunderbolt 4 (USB Type-C) bağlantı noktası ve evrensel ses jakı bulunuyor; ancak cihazda yerleşik HDMI bağlantı noktası, USB-A girişi veya SD kart okuyucu yer almıyor.

**Neden önemli?** Yeni Dell XPS 14 (2026), günlük kullanımda şarj cihazı taşıma zorunluluğunu ortadan kaldıran pil ömrü ve yeni nesil pil hücreleriyle dizüstü bilgisayar pazarında dikkat çekici bir alternatif oluşturuyor.

sources.title: Dell’s new XPS 14 tackles battery anxiety with all-day power

source_texts.title: Dell’s new XPS 14 tackles battery anxiety with all-day power
source_texts.summary: The XPS 14 is back for 2026 , and Dell hasn’t simply pulled the old model out of storage. It has a redesigned aluminum chassis, physical function keys, and newer Intel processors.
source_texts.text:
The XPS 14 is back for 2026, and Dell hasn’t simply pulled the old model out of storage. It has a redesigned aluminum chassis, physical function keys, and newer Intel processors.
At 3 pounds and 14.62mm thick, it still remains impressively thin and lightweight, like what we've come to expect from Dell XPS laptops. That said, battery life is the biggest highlight this time.
The Dell XPS 14’s battery life stands out
Dell XPS 14 (2026)
- CPU
- Up to Intel® Core Ultra X9 Processor 388H (16- Core, 18MB Cache, up to 5.1 GHz)
- Display (Size, Resolution)
- 14-inch, 2K (1920 x 1200)
- RAM
- 16GB LPDDR5x Dual Channel at 7467 MT/s 32GB LPDDR5x Dual Channel at 9600 MT/s 64GB LPDDR5x Dual Channel at 9600 MT/s
- Storage
- 512GB PCIe 4 SSD (Gen 4) 1TB PCIe 4 SSD (Gen 4) 2TB PCIe 4 SSD (Gen 5, SED ready) 4TB PCIe 4 SSD (Gen 5, SED ready)
- Battery
- 70Whr battery (integrated), 900ED cells ExpressCharge 1.0
- Ports
- 3x Thunderbolt 4 (USB Type-C ) with DisplayPort 2.1 and Power Delivery Kensington lock supported via USB Type-C ports Universal audio jack
The Dell XPS 14 (2026) is built for long days of work, classes, and entertainment without constantly searching for an outlet. Its standout battery life makes it a compelling choice if you want a premium laptop that keeps up with your day and handles your everyday tasks with ease.
- Operating System
- Windows 11
- Webcam
- 8MP/1080p HDR webcam Windows Hello compliant, Intel IPU7
- Dimensions
- 12.19x8.26x0.58in
- Weight
- 3 pounds
- NPU
- Intel® AI Boost NPU 47 TOPs on 325, 49 TOPs on 355, 50 TOPs on 358H & 388H
Dell says the XPS 14 can last up to a whopping 31 hours of streaming with the 2K display and brightness set to 250 nits, giving it the best battery life of any 14-inch notebook currently on sale.
In XDA’s review, the Dell XPS 14 comfortably lasted through eight hours of regular use, with the Intel® Core™ Ultra 7 processor model hitting a staggering 25 hours in the Procyon productivity test. Only the dual-screen Zenbook Duo managed better numbers in XDA’s reviews, but even that model comes with a larger battery (99Wh vs 70Wh) and a bulkier chassis than the XPS 14.
Whether you're a student or a working professional, the new XPS 14 is the kind of laptop you can take to work, class, or a full day of meetings without automatically packing the charger. You can spend more time moving between rooms or working away from your desk without planning the day around the nearest outlet.
It starts with Dell’s new 900ED battery cells
Interestingly, Dell didn’t achieve the impressive battery-life numbers by packing in an oversized battery. The XPS 14 has a 70Wh battery that keeps the laptop thin enough to carry every day. The secret is what’s inside.
The XPS 14 (2026) is the first laptop to use 900ED battery cells, which Dell describes as an industry high for energy density. Put simply, the cells can store more energy without requiring a larger and heavier battery pack. As a result, the XPS 14 measures just 14.62mm thick and starts at 3 pounds, despite carrying a battery large enough for a premium performance laptop.
A display that balances sharpness, speed, and battery life
Dell offers two display options for the XPS 14. The standard 2K panel is non-touch, reaches 500 nits, and supports a variable refresh rate of up to 120Hz. It isn’t the most colorful option, but it is sharp enough for a 14-inch screen and decreases to a 1Hz refresh rate to save battery power.
Dell also offers an optional 2.8K tandem OLED touchscreen that delivers deeper blacks, richer colors, and the contrast you would expect from an OLED panel, while keeping a smooth 120Hz refresh rate. However, it only goes down to a 20Hz refresh rate.
Intel’s latest processors bring plenty of power
The XPS 14 is available with Intel’s latest Intel® Core™ Ultra Series 3 processors.
Pricing starts at $2,249.99. Buyers can configure the XPS 14 with an Intel® Core™ Ultra 7 355 processor, 16GB of RAM, 512GB of storage, and a 2K display for $2,249.99 or upgrade to an OLED touchscreen with Core Ultra X7 358H, 32GB of RAM, and a 1TB SSD for $3,149.99. Meanwhile, the maxed-out Core Ultra X9 388H model with 64GB of RAM and 2TB of storage reaches $4,999.99.
For everyday use, the Intel® Core™ Ultra 7 355 offers plenty of performance. Buyers who regularly edit photos and videos or want more graphics power should consider the Intel® Core™ Ultra X7 358 or Core Ultra X9, which come with more capable integrated Intel Arc B390 graphics, considering there is no discrete GPU option like the previous model.
The processors also include an NPU for Copilot+ PC features and supported AI workloads. It can handle features such as Windows Studio Effects without relying entirely on the processor or integrated GPU, which is particularly useful during video calls.
Windows 11 comes with a modern design and multitasking tools to help you get it done faster, easier, and with style.
The new design feels more like the XPS we wanted
Dell clearly listened to criticism of its previous premium laptops. The capacitive function buttons are gone, with a proper physical function row taking their place. That makes shortcuts easier to find without looking at the keyboard.
The gap-less keyboard can still take some adjustment, especially if you prefer more space between the keys. However, the aluminum chassis feels suitably premium, while the Gorilla Glass palm rest and seamless haptic touchpad give the interior a clean, modern finish.
Dell has also included an 8MP webcam capable of recording 4K HDR video. The four-speaker system delivers up to 10W of audio output, while Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.0 cover wireless connectivity.
You’ll probably need a dongle
The XPS 14 has three Thunderbolt 4 ports with DisplayPort 2.1 and Power Delivery, along with a universal audio jack. You can charge it from either side and connect multiple high-resolution displays, but there is no built-in HDMI port, USB-A connection, or SD card reader.
That won’t be an issue if your accessories already use USB-C or you normally work from a dock. However, some competing premium laptops and even the cheaper Dell 14S offer a broader port selection, and photographers or creators may miss the built-in card reader.
The right XPS 14 can leave the charger at home
The OLED model will attract plenty of attention, and understandably so. But for most buyers, the 2K XPS 14 is the smarter pick. It combines a 3-pound design, a sharp 1-120Hz variable refresh rate display, modern Intel hardware, and enough battery life to comfortably cover a full working day.
Dell has made the XPS 14 thinner, lighter, and more practical than its predecessor. It feels like the return to form the lineup needed, and its excellent battery life makes this more than a comeback in name only.
